digest.top_line: STAMPEDE meta-analysis: 2yr abiraterone + ADT/RT in high-risk M0 cuts metastasis risk near half (MFS HR 0.53, OS HR 0.60); enza adds toxicity only.
digest.tldr: Prostate carries the day, and it lands squarely on the RT clinic: 85% of the 1974 pts had RT planned (74Gy/37fx or hypofx equivalent), so this is an intensification question layered on definitive local therapy, not a systemic-only one. 6yr MFS 82% vs 69%, OS 86% vs 77%. Enza on top: interaction HR 1.02, G3+ 58% vs 37%.

sites.intro: High-risk M0 disease treated with definitive RT + ADT: the open question is which agent to add, and at what toxicity cost.

studies.name: STAMPEDE (abiraterone ± enzalutamide, high-risk non-metastatic)
studies.tldr: MFS HR 0.53 (0.44-0.64) and OS HR 0.60 adding 2yr abiraterone to ADT+RT in high-risk M0; enzalutamide adds nothing.
details: 🔍 Two open-label phase 3 STAMPEDE trials, non-overlapping controls, IPD meta-analysis; N=1974, 113 UK/Swiss sites, median f/u 72mo
🔍 RT mandated for N0, encouraged for N+: 74Gy/37fx to prostate + SV or hypofractionated equivalent
📊 RT planned in 1684 (85%) of 1974; 99% of newly diagnosed N0, 71% of N+, 7% of previously treated
📐 6yr MFS 82% (79-85) combination vs 69% (66-72) control; 6yr OS 86% vs 77%
📊 Secondary endpoints, combination vs control (all p<0.0001)
📊 MFS by prespecified stratification subgroup (forest, Fig 3)
📐 Enza adds nothing: interaction HR 1.02 (0.70-1.50), p=0.91; between-trial heterogeneity I² p=0.90

details.text: ⚠️ Enza costs toxicity without efficacy (G3+ within 24mo, combination vs control)
subdetails: Grade 5: 3 in abi group, 4 in abi+enza group, none in controls

details: ⚠️ Open label; toxicity reported only during first 2yrs of treatment; subsequent-therapy data called unreliable by authors
⚠️ Relapsing-after-local-therapy pts under-represented; authors flag benefit uncertain in that group
⚠️ PS 1-2 and NSAID/aspirin heterogeneity (p=0.0052) has no biological explanation; authors say it should not change management

verdict.rationale: Two prospectively randomised phase 3 trials, prespecified pooled MFS primary hit, 72mo f/u, applicable population. Authors' own conclusion: new standard alongside ADT and RT.
verdict.audience: High-risk non-metastatic prostate: N+ or N0 with 2 of T3-4/Gleason 8-10/PSA ≥40

studies.significance: This is an RT-population trial: 85% were planned for 74Gy/37fx or hypofractionated equivalent, and benefit was identical whether RT was planned (HR 0.54, 0.44-0.67) or not (0.51, 0.34-0.76). So the 2yr abiraterone layers onto 3yr ADT plus definitive RT without an RT-related interaction, and N+ pts (39% of cohort) did at least as well (HR 0.49) as N0.
studies.monday_clinic: In high-risk M0 disease heading for definitive RT with long-course ADT (N+, or N0 with two of T3-4 / Gleason 8-10 / PSA ≥40), this supports intensifying the hormonal backbone with 2yr abiraterone rather than adding enzalutamide; it does not extend to post-prostatectomy pts or to relapse after prior local therapy, both under-represented.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Two **open-label phase 3** randomised trials inside the STAMPEDE MAMS platform with the same eligibility and **no overlapping controls**, pooled by IPD meta-analysis. 113 UK and Swiss sites, recruitment Nov 15 2011 to March 31 2016, median follow-up **72 months** (IQR 63-73). Primary outcome was switched from OS to MFS for the non-metastatic population before any efficacy inspection, approved by the independent trial steering committee Dec 2 2019.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: High-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer: **node positive**, or node negative with at least **two of T3-T4, Gleason 8-10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL**, or relapsing with high-risk features. WHO PS 0-2, no age limit, clinically significant cardiovascular disease excluded. N=1974; median age 68, median PSA 34 ng/mL, **774 (39%) node positive**, 1563 (79%) of 1968 Gleason 8-10.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **ADT for 3 years** in all arms. Combination arms added oral **abiraterone acetate 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg daily for 2 years**, and in the second trial **enzalutamide 160 mg daily** as well. Median time on abiraterone was 23.7 months alone vs 20.7 months with enzalutamide; 266 (59%) of 451 vs 222 (43%) of 513 stopped for planned completion.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Local RT **74 Gy in 37 fractions to prostate and seminal vesicles** (or hypofractionated equivalent) was **mandated for node-negative** and encouraged for node-positive disease. Planned RT rate was **1684 (85%) of 1974**: 99% of newly diagnosed N0, 71% of N+, 7% of previously treated. Where RT was omitted, combination therapy could run until progression instead of stopping at 2 years.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: metastasis-free survival.** Secondary: overall survival, prostate cancer-specific survival, biochemical failure-free survival, progression-free survival, toxicity. Powered at 90% (one-sided alpha 1.25%) to detect **HR 0.75**, requiring roughly 315 control-group MFS events.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: 180 MFS events in combination arms vs 306 in controls, **HR 0.53**. Effect held separately in each trial (abiraterone 0.54, abiraterone plus enzalutamide 0.53) with **no added benefit from enzalutamide** (interaction HR 1.02, p=0.91). Proportional hazards held for MFS (p=0.46) and OS (p=0.10).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Adding enzalutamide roughly doubled the G3+ burden: **58% vs 32%** in the abiraterone plus enzalutamide trial against **37% vs 29%** in the abiraterone trial. Hypertension, fatigue and transaminase rise drove the difference. Seven grade 5 events, none in controls.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Prior abiraterone plus enzalutamide or apalutamide combinations in mCRPC showed only modest rPFS gains with no OS benefit, which the investigators cite as the prespecified reason they expected no separation between the two trials here. The indirect comparison cannot exclude a small enzalutamide effect, but **the added toxicity and cost are not justified**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents high-risk M0 prostate cancer starting at least 3 years of ADT, mostly node positive or T3-T4 Gleason 8-10, with definitive prostate RT planned in 85%. Does not represent pts relapsing after prior local therapy (under-represented) or men treated with prostatectomy plus combination therapy, which the protocol did not test.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Open-label design means control pts could access second-generation hormone therapy for M0 CRPC in trials or, since 2019, as SOC, which would bias OS toward the null rather than away. Toxicity was captured only for the first 24 months, so late cardiovascular and metabolic effects of 2yr abiraterone are not characterised. Subsequent-therapy data are described by the authors as unreliable.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The **2 year** duration was pragmatic, chosen to match the ADT duration required with RT, not optimised; shorter could suffice and longer might do more. An androgen receptor antagonist alone added to ADT plus RT was never tested here, leaving that cheaper intensification unanswered.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 85% of this cohort was planned for 74Gy/37fx (or hypofractionated equivalent) with 3yr ADT, so this is your patient. Benefit was flat across the RT-planned (HR 0.54, 0.44-0.67) and RT-omitted (0.51, 0.34-0.76) strata, and N+ pts, who got RT only 71% of the time, still reached HR 0.49. Nothing here changes dose or target volume, it changes the systemic backbone you prescribe alongside.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Two years of abiraterone plus prednisolone on top of 3yr ADT is the intensification that works in M0; layering enzalutamide gave interaction HR 1.02 (0.70-1.50) while doubling G3+ events to 58%. PCSS HR 0.49 and bFFS HR 0.39 argue the effect is real disease control, not lead-time. WHO PS 1-2 pts showed attenuated MFS benefit (HR 0.86, 0.58-1.28).
